# Analyze the relationship between introduction pathways and mrt in the invasion_success dataset
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Check the distribution of mrt across different introduction pathways
sns.boxplot(x='intro.pathway', y='mrt', data=invasion_success)
plt.title('Distribution of Minimum Residence Time (mrt) by Introduction Pathway')
plt.xlabel('Introduction Pathway')
plt.ylabel('Minimum Residence Time (mrt)')
plt.show()

# Check for statistical significance using ANOVA
from scipy.stats import f_oneway

# Filter out rows with missing values in 'mrt' and 'intro.pathway'
filtered_data = invasion_success.dropna(subset=['mrt', 'intro.pathway'])

# Group the data by 'intro.pathway' and extract the 'mrt' values
groups = filtered_data.groupby('intro.pathway')['mrt'].apply(list)

# Perform ANOVA
f_statistic, p_value = f_oneway(*groups)
f_statistic, p_value

# Analyze the relationship between mrt and invasion success metrics (e.g., number.of.invaded.plots)
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Scatter plot of mrt vs. number.of.invaded.plots
sns.scatterplot(x='mrt', y='number.of.invaded.plots', data=invasion_success)
plt.title('Relationship between Minimum Residence Time (mrt) and Number of Invaded Plots')
plt.xlabel('Minimum Residence Time (mrt)')
plt.ylabel('Number of Invaded Plots')
plt.show()

# Perform linear regression to quantify the relationship
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression

# Prepare the data for regression
X = invasion_success[['mrt']].values.reshape(-1, 1)  # Predictor
y = invasion_success['number.of.invaded.plots'].values  # Response

# Create a linear regression model
model = LinearRegression()
model.fit(X, y)

# Get the coefficient and R-squared value
coefficient = model.coef_[0]
r_squared = model.score(X, y)
coefficient, r_squared

# Perform multiple regression analysis with mrt and introduction pathway as predictors
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression

# Prepare the data for multiple regression
X = invasion_success[['mrt', 'intro.pathway']].copy()
X = pd.get_dummies(X, columns=['intro.pathway'])  # One-hot encode the pathway variable
y = invasion_success['number.of.invaded.plots'].values  # Response

# Create a linear regression model
model = LinearRegression()
model.fit(X, y)

# Get the coefficients and R-squared value
coefficients = model.coef_
r_squared = model.score(X, y)
coefficients, r_squared
